description:
CausalReport exposes five pieces of surface consumed by exactly one file each, all src/telemetry/public_trace_test.rs:

  .product_publications   1 use
  .final_population       4 uses
  .lifecycles             3 uses
  .shifts                 1 use
  derive_requests()       5 uses

Compare the load-bearing surface, which has two or three independent consumers: .uncaused (17 uses, the north-star invariant), formula_totals/product_totals (10/9, pinned per-fixture work counts), canonical_multiset (6, the cross-run comparand), .sessions (19), .formulas, .products.

Being one-consumer-deep is NOT automatically waste. .lifecycles carries the retract-and-remint signature (first_appearances > distinct) and .undefined_first_uses proves the self-describing-stream contract; those are real invariants that happen to need one assertion each. The question is whether each field earns a record type, or whether the assertion could read what it needs from an existing one.

For each of the five: name the invariant it exists to prove, or delete it with its assertion. Record the answer next to the type so the next scan does not re-raise it.

Sequence after fz-0am and fz-foq.3: the arc changes which records exist and the move changes where they live. Judging the surface before both would judge a shape that is about to change.
title: Justify or drop the one-assertion-deep report surface
